content.text: After I fixed the CSV problem, I tested with this netcdf file. It uploaded correctly and looks like a binary. However, when I go to download it, I simply get the filename versus the data in the file.   Odd behavior and needs to be looked into further.
Actually, I had run the curl command wrong.  When I do it the correct way, I am able to create a binary with the nc file type as well as retrieve it successfully.
– what version of fedora are you using?  (or hyrax).
(to be clear, it works after I fixed the csv issue, so that fix might have fixed the nc issue as well).
Your change is not yet in a version that we can upgrade to, right?
No - it's not in the code base yet (still a PR).   It should end up in fedora 4.7.4 once that's released.
: are you in a position to verify the fix if we provide a war file?

Are you in a position to verify that you no longer see this issue using that release?
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing.  It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.

After ingesting an nc (application/netcdf, application/x-netcdf) file and a csv file the system could not retrieve them. The version of fits I'm using may be returning multiple possible mime-types, and then Fedora is accepting them, but not retuning them.

I've attached the nc file I used. I'm also attaching the backtrace I get when I try to access an nc file from the browser using Fedora (backtrace.txt), and one for the csv file (csv_fedora_backtrace.txt).

comments.body:
Partially resolved with https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1205

After I fixed the CSV problem, I tested with this netcdf file. It uploaded correctly and looks like a binary. However, when I go to download it, I simply get the filename versus the data in the file.   Odd behavior and needs to be looked into further.

Actually, I had run the curl command wrong.  When I do it the correct way, I am able to create a binary with the nc file type as well as retrieve it successfully.  

 

Jose Blanco – what version of fedora are you using?  (or hyrax).  

(to be clear, it works after I fixed the csv issue, so that fix might have fixed the nc issue as well).

Fedora 4.5.1 and Hyrax 1.0.1

 

Your change is not yet in a version that we can upgrade to, right?
No - it's not in the code base yet (still a PR).   It should end up in fedora 4.7.4 once that's released.
Jose Blanco: are you in a position to verify the fix if we provide a war file?

Hi Jose Blanco – this fix is now in the 4.7.4 release.

Are you in a position to verify that you no longer see this issue using that release?
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing. It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.
